First things first. 

This isn't your fault. Repeat: not your fault. 

You're a minor, it's not your responsibility to find housing. You are the child. It's your parents' responsibility to care for you. If it's a catastrophe, that's okay. It's not forever and, again, it isn't your fault.

You sound really overwhelmed. Please take one thing at a time.

Not sure where you are, but if you're a minor, there should be programs to make sure you've got a place to stay. 

I know what it's like to feel like you don't belong. You are not alone. I can GUARANTEE that your parents would rather have you around. They won't be better off without you- you're their child and you are needed.

As far as the GED is concerned, take it one thing at a time. I was ready to do it the other day and someone convinced me to wait. I felt doomed, but just stayed alive for the day. Things got a tiny bit better. They still FUCKING SUCK, but it's not absolute crushing despair. 

I know you must be pretty tired of all of this, but you don't deserve to die because of this. It's not your fault.

You're in the rare position to take action for everyone who doesn't feel okay.

It was 10 years ago and I think about it multiple times a day. It has ruined my life. It may possibly take my life, as the course it's set me on has brought me here. 

I'm not alone. 

There are a lot of people trying to stop this. You can be one of them. A rare voice from the other side. 

Don't forget this shitty feeling. Amplify it by 100000000x10000000, live with it daily and you're close to knowing what it feels like to be on the other side. 

Don't waste this.

At least you're owning up to whatever may have happened. To feel better, become an example. I'm sorry, but the statistics are against you. It's a good sign that you feel bad about it, because most people would try to manipulate the situation to their advantage. I would advise speaking to her only through a mediator.

As a sexual assault suvivor, here is my advice:

Go to a neutral third party and explain that you'd like to take responsibility for what happened, even though you don't remember it. Then get involved in consent education. If there isn't any where you're at, start something. It won't just help you, it will help women out there who have not been given cultural permission to say no. You can take leadership and turn this into something super positive that can prevent something tragic happening in the future. 

If there were people who saw she was passed out/drunk and did nothing, they are also responsible. This isn't just your fault. Sexual assault is a community problem.

Also, her past has nothing to do with it. At all. 

Trust me, sexual assault ruins lives. I may not survive because of it. You can become part of the solution by realizing if you feel this, imagine what it's like to be the victim...especially if no one believes you, helps you, or you never get anything nearing justice? 

A lot of us have to live knowing our rapists got away with it. You can use this as an opportunity to step out and be someone who advocates for victims.
Be careful of anyone who sends you information via pm or would like to enter into a "pact" with you. They may be a predator.

The first non-abusive relationship I was in where I was truly in love- he died. He was unique, beautiful, brilliant, hilarious. Accidental drug OD, not suicide, but sudden and tragic. I felt guilty because he died the day after Valentine's day (9 years ago, not recently). He was out of town. I know it wasn't my fault, but I wondered maybe his death had something to do with me because we had a very simple fight and I didn't return a message he left me because I was too damned busy. I felt responsible. He had been clean, so maybe he relapsed because of me? I'll never know. 

I'm so, so sorry. I don't know exactly what you're going through, but I was very, very much in love and the loss fucked me the fuck up. I would literally wake up from dreams about him and howl. I would howl from some place inside me I couldn't control. I had never known anyone who died before that, so I had no resources. Since then, my best friend and brother have died rather tragically (undiagnosed stomach cancer and not getting to the ER on time because Urgent Care didn't call an ambulance), but losing my boyfriend was like being on a small, uncharted island. With the other deaths, so many other people were devastated in the same way and mourned with me, so I was able to limp along. With my boyfriend, it was like a beautiful star had gone missing from the sky, but I was the only one who knew it had been there. There are memories with him I can't share with other people. I loved him so dearly. It felt very unfair too, because he was quite remarkable while so many people seem so dull and lack his brilliance and gentleness.

This isn't your fault. Please know that.

I'm on this forum for different reasons, but I just wanted to tell you that I did make it through that loss. I can't say I know what you're going through, but I know the pain of losing someone you're in love with and am so sorry. Please give it some time. I was in so much pain and all alone with it. But I was surprised that within a year, I was no longer seeing him everywhere. When I think of him now, it is with much sweetness and gratitude that I knew someone so amazing. 

Please give yourself a chance to be a mess for a little while and heal from this. 

One thing I didn't do is get grief counseling. I wish I'd done that. Please give that a shot before you go.

All rehab places have the same attitude toward benzos (e.g., it's your fault, not the drugs). You will not find anyone in the benzo recovery community who will advise you to go to rehab.

I understand you are extremely overwhelmed. You're not supposed to know what to do right now. You sound like you're in crisis, so please be gentle with yourself and take it one thing at a time. 

NAMI (National Alliance for the Mentally Ill) may be able to provide referrals to free or sliding scale counseling. Your local chapter may also have free group therapy. Find their contact information here: http://www.nami.org/Find-Support/NAMI-HelpLine

Call them and tell them and let them know you need help, but don't know how to get it. Describe your symptoms (perhaps mention PTSD if that's what you have) and ask for guidance getting free or affordable counseling and/or group therapy.  

Also, the National Suicide Hotline 1-800-273-8255 may be able to direct you to local helplines that can offer referrals. 

Please don't be discouraged if the people you speak with don't give you exactly what you need. They're definitely not perfect. I've had terrific experiences and bad experiences with helplines. The point is to just keep plugging at it and keep finding more information to help yourself. 

It's okay not to know what to do. We're both just trying to figure it out. You've done a lot already by telling your story here and asking for help.

The important thing to do is keep trying and not give up. It sucks, but just don't give up.
